title: Revision of plant pest temporary prohibition lists
summary: EU adds Mexican cabbage head caterpillar and darkling beetle to list of prohibited pests, and extends listing …
update:
The European Union (EU) has added Mexican cabbage head caterpillar ( Copitarsia decolora ) and darkling beetle ( Lagria villosa ) to its list of prohibited pests, and has extended the listing of three further prohibited pests.

In total, there are now six pests on the EU list of temporarily prohibited plant pests.
impacted_products: Alfalfa, apple, asparagus, aubergine (eggplant), banana/plantain, broccoli, cabbage, cauliflower, chickpea, citrus, coffee, common bean, cucumber, garlic, grapevine, lettuce, maize, onion, peach, peanut, pear, persimmon, pineapple, potato, rice, sorghum, soyabean, stone fruit, strawberry, sunflower, sweet cherry, tanbark, tea, tobacco, tomato, wheat
what_changing: The EU regularly updates the list of pests that are temporarily prohibited from introduction into the EU on the basis of available scientific evidence. The list is published in the Annex of Regulation 2022/1941 .
why:
Mexican cabbage head caterpillar ( C. decolora ) and darkling beetle ( L. villosa ) have been repeatedly intercepted in consignments of plants and plant products imported into the EU from non-EU countries. They are not known to occur in the EU, and preliminary risk assessments conducted by Spain and the Netherlands ( NVWA 2025 ) concluded that they present a high phytosanitary risk and may meet the criteria for Union quarantine pests. The temporary prohibition will remain in place while complete pest risk assessments are conducted.

The removal of L. pseudorbonalis from the list in 2025 followed evaluations by the European Food Safety Authority ( EFSA 2024a , 2024b ).

The list of regulated pests is updated on an ongoing basis according to the most recent scientific evaluations.
timeline: The revised list of prohibited pests applies from 30 July 2026 .
background:
Regulation 2022/1941 prohibits the introduction, movement, holding, multiplication, or release of certain pests within the EU territory.

When EU Member States notify the European Commission of the presence in consignments of new pests that are not listed as Union quarantine pests, but pose a significant risk, these pests are temporarily included in the list pending further assessment and potential addition to Annex II of Regulation 2019/2072 .
